name: Southwest Slopes / Lucky Pass

waypoints.name: Thunder Creek Trailhead (Colonial Creek Campground, South Loop)
waypoints.note: This is a legitimately long/remote approach (24-mile round trip: Thunder Creek Trail to McAllister camp, off-trail to Borealis Lake, across Borealis Glacier to Lucky Pass)
waypoints.directions: Colonial Creek Campground sits on SR-20 at Diablo Lake, milepost 130, roughly 25 miles east of Marblemount. Turn in on the campground's south side and park in the large lot above the boat ramp, around 1,240 ft. That lot is also the Thunder Creek Trailhead, and the maintained Thunder Creek Trail runs south from it.

waypoints.name: Thunder Creek log crossing
waypoints.note: The original footbridge over Thunder Creek near mile 6.6 washed out in fall 2017; parties cross via a log felled about 1,000 ft downstream of the old bridge site. Coordinates approximate.

waypoints.name: McAllister Camp
waypoints.note: Backcountry stock camp where McAllister Creek meets Thunder Creek; leave the maintained trail here and pick up the unmaintained climbers' boot path at the first fork. Coordinates approximate.

waypoints.name: Ridge viewpoint
waypoints.note: Boot path up the north ridge passes a viewpoint here with the first views of Primus, Tricouni, and neighboring peaks. Coordinates approximate.

waypoints.name: Borealis Lake camp
waypoints.note: Standard base camp on a flat bench below the Borealis Glacier. Elevation and coordinates are approximate — not precisely surveyed.

waypoints.name: Lucky Pass (Primus-Tricouni col)
waypoints.note: Reached via roped travel across the Borealis Glacier's west edge, which has retreated and split into upper/lower tiers separated by slabs and cliffs. Elevation and coordinates are approximate.

approach: Start at Colonial Creek Campground on SR-20 (Diablo Lake, milepost 130, roughly 25 miles east of Marblemount) and park in the large lot above the boat ramp on the campground's south side — this is also the Thunder Creek Trailhead. Follow the maintained Thunder Creek Trail south about 6.5-6.7 miles to McAllister Camp (~1,900 ft), a backcountry stock camp where McAllister Creek meets Thunder Creek. The trail's original bridge over Thunder Creek near mile 6.6 washed out in fall 2017; parties now cross via a log felled roughly 1,000 ft downstream of the old bridge site (about 900 ft upstream of the Thunder/McAllister Creek confluence). At McAllister Camp, leave the maintained trail and pick up the unmaintained climbers' boot path at the first fork, climbing steeply through brush and around downed timber up the north ridge; a viewpoint near 4,600 ft gives the first look at Primus, Tricouni, and neighboring peaks. Continue through forest and heather to Borealis Lake (base camp), a flat bench below the Borealis Glacier. From camp, rope up for glacier travel and follow the west edge of the Borealis Glacier — which has retreated significantly and split into upper and lower tiers separated by slabs and cliffs — navigating crevasses to Lucky Pass, the Primus-Tricouni col. From Lucky Pass, climb a steep snow finger roughly 200 ft up Tricouni's southwest side, then transition to rock ramps and ledges (class 3-4 scrambling) up the west ridge to the bouldery 8,102 ft summit. Hazards: crevasses on the Borealis Glacier (worse late season), a brushy and poorly marked boot path above McAllister Camp, and afternoon softening of the snow finger.

approach_variants.name: Thunder Creek, Borealis Lake and Lucky Pass
approach_variants.notes: From the large lot above the boat ramp at Colonial Creek, follow the maintained Thunder Creek Trail south to McAllister Camp; the old bridge near mile 6.6 is gone and the crossing is now a log felled downstream of the old site. At the camp leave the maintained trail and pick up the unmaintained boot path at the first fork, climbing steeply through brush and blowdown up the north ridge past a viewpoint that gives the first look at the peaks. Continue through forest and heather to the flat bench at Borealis Lake, the base camp. From camp rope up and follow the west edge of the Borealis Glacier, which has retreated into an upper and a lower tier separated by slabs and cliffs, to the col.
approach_variants.season: July and August are best; earlier ascents need ice technique, and the south-facing snow above the col softens dangerously through the day
hazards: Crevasses on the Borealis Glacier, worse late in the season
Brushy, poorly marked boot path above McAllister Camp
Afternoon softening of the south-facing snow finger — start early
Class 3-4 rock ramps and ledges above the snow
approach_variants.baseFinding: Lucky Pass, the col between Primus and this peak, is the base, and which way you turn on it is the whole test. Standing on the col, Primus is the peak to the east and this one is to the west; the route turns west. Above the pass on that side a single steep snow finger runs up roughly 200 ft. It is unmistakable from the col and there is no second candidate, and it is the entry to the climb. Above the snow the ground becomes rock ramps and ledges, class 3 to 4, following the west ridge to a bouldery summit. If you have left the col heading east onto a broad class 2-3 ridge, you are climbing Primus instead. If you are still threading crevasses on slabby, tiered ice below the col, you have not reached the pass at all — the glacier here is split into two tiers by slabs and cliffs and it is the upper tier that runs to the col.

pitch_detail.notes: Thunder Creek Trailhead (Colonial Creek Campground) to McAllister Camp on the maintained Thunder Creek Trail; ~6.5-6.7 mi.
Unmaintained boot path up the north ridge from McAllister Camp, past a 4,600 ft viewpoint, to Borealis Lake camp below the glacier.
Roped crossing of the Borealis Glacier's west edge (retreated, split into upper/lower tiers separated by slabs and cliffs) to Lucky Pass, the Primus-Tricouni col.
Steep snow finger (~200 ft) up Tricouni's southwest side, then rock ramps/ledges (Class 3-4) up the west ridge to the summit.

access.fees: $10 per person plus a $6 reservation fee for advance permits (youth 15 and under free); no park entrance fee at North Cascades NP.
access.notes: 60% of sites (Boston Basin/Eldorado/Sulphide Glacier/etc.) are reservable in advance via Recreation.gov (2026 lottery Mar 2–13); the remaining 40% are walk-up, obtained in person the day before at the Wilderness Information Center in Marblemount.
access.rules: Group size capped at 6 in off-trail cross-country zones (12 in on-trail corridors). Boston Basin camping restricted to two designated sites (Low Camp ~5,300 ft, High Camp ~6,400 ft). Bear canisters required in some zones — free loaners at permit offices.
access.permit: Overnight backcountry/wilderness permit required year-round for any camping on this route. About 60% of designated camps/zones are reservable in advance on Recreation.gov (requires watching a safety video and emailing the WIC within 3 days of your trip to confirm); the park holds roughly 40% of sites for walk-up permits issued in person at the WIC (Marblemount) or Glacier Public Service Center, day-of or day-before only.
access.closures: Colonial Creek Campground and the Thunder Creek Trailhead are reached via SR-20, which stays open essentially year-round this far west (well before the highway's seasonal closure gate near Ross Dam, MP 134); Cascade River Road to Eldorado Creek is not needed for this route unless linking into the Inspiration Traverse. The original Thunder Creek Trail bridge near mile 6.6 washed out in fall 2017 and has not been replaced — parties cross via a log felled downstream of the old bridge site.
access.seasonal: SR-20 stays open to Colonial Creek Campground year-round; the highway's winter closure is further east near Ross Dam.
access.landManager: North Cascades National Park (NPS) — Wilderness Information Center, Marblemount, WA, (360) 854-7245, noca_wilderness@nps.gov
access.land_manager: National Park Service — North Cascades National Park (Stephen Mather Wilderness)
access.passRequired: No entrance pass needed; wilderness camping permit is mandatory for overnight trips.

overnight_permit.what: North Cascades NP wilderness permit — limited, with a fee
overnight_permit.where: Reserve on Recreation.gov, or get a walk-up permit in person at the Marblemount Wilderness Information Center up to a day ahead. Camps above Thunder Creek fall in cross-country zones.

itinerary.cal: Glacier travel and the snow chute are typically climbable only once the Borealis Glacier consolidates in mid-to-late summer (roughly July-September); the Thunder Creek Trail itself is accessible earlier.

days.note: A long trail-plus-bushwhack day: hike the maintained Thunder Creek Trail to McAllister Camp, then pick up a boot path climbing the ridge toward the Borealis Glacier to a flat camp near Borealis Lake. Parties in trip reports often arrive at camp mid-afternoon, well ahead of schedule.
days.title: Thunder Creek approach to Borealis camp

schedule.label: Leave Thunder Creek Trailhead
schedule.detail: Follow the maintained Thunder Creek Trail south.

schedule.label: Reach McAllister Camp
schedule.detail: 6.5 trail miles in; pick up the climbers' boot path here.

schedule.label: Climb the ridge to Borealis Glacier
schedule.detail: Off-trail ascent through brush and heather to timberline.

schedule.label: Make camp near Borealis Lake
schedule.detail: Flat bench below the glacier used as the standard base camp.

days.objective: Reach a camp on the Borealis Ridge/Lake bench below the glacier

days.note: From camp, rope up and cross the Borealis Glacier to Lucky Pass (the Primus-Tricouni col), then climb a snow chute and class 2-3 rock/scree on the peak's south/southwest side to the summit. Round-trip from camp back to the same camp.
days.title: Summit day via Borealis Glacier and Lucky Pass

schedule.label: Leave camp
schedule.detail: Start early to have firm glacier snow and beat afternoon softening/storms.

schedule.label: Cross Borealis Glacier to Lucky Pass
schedule.detail: Glacier travel roped up; watch for crevasses.

schedule.label: Ascend snow chute below the summit
schedule.detail: Steep snow finger gaining the southwest ridge/face.

schedule.label: Summit Tricouni Peak (8,102 ft)
schedule.detail: Class 2-3 scrambling on solid rock for the final pitch; some parties linger up to an hour on top.

schedule.label: Reverse route to camp
schedule.detail: Descend the chute and re-cross the glacier back to Borealis Lake camp.

days.objective: Climb Tricouni Peak and return to camp

days.note: Break camp and descend the ridge boot path back to McAllister Camp, then follow the Thunder Creek Trail out. Weather often turns on the way out, so an early start is common.
days.title: Hike out to trailhead

itinerary.totalNote: A 3-day, ~24-mile round trip with one base camp near Borealis Lake; roughly 6,900 ft of gain overall, with the middle day given to the roped glacier/snow summit push.
